item.title: Swiss companies aim to make Tesla’s Cybertruck road-legal in Europe
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Werk.lab and Revoltaris are working to get the Tesla Cybertruck approved for Swiss certification. To achieve this, the electric pickup had to undergo technical revisions in several areas.

item.title: India: Bihar Police to deploy 1,100 electric motorcycles
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: The police department of Bihar, a state in the eastern part of India, plans to deploy 1,100 electric motorcycles for patrolling operations. It has ordered these vehicles from Revolt Motors, one of the few electric motorcycle manufacturers in the country.

item.title: Quehenberger doubles its battery-electric truck fleet
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Austrian logistics company Quehenberger is further expanding its electric truck fleet. By the end of 2026, the company - which operates for the drugstore chain dm, among others - will nearly double the number of its own e-trucks from 13 to 24 alongside building the necessary charging infrastructure.

item.title: UK BEV registrations reach annual high with 32 per cent market share
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Registrations of new battery-electric cars rose by 32.7 per cent year-on-year in October, reaching 48,858 units. That's according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT), which said BEVs accounted for 32 per cent of the market - their highest share so far this year.

item.title: Kia EV2 Earth: Two weeks with Kia’s compact range marvel
item.dc:creator: Robin Engelhardt
item.description: A longstanding rule of thumb in electromobility has been that you either get long range or compact dimensions - you can't have both, especially not at an attractive price. After all, the battery has to fit somewhere. Kia wants to change that with its new EV2. This 4.06-meter-long compact car is available with an optional 61-kWh battery and a starting price tag of €26,600. We tested it for two weeks and were positively surprised by how the Koreans have created a genuinely attractive overall package using very simple means.

item.title: Kia EV7 and H2-Carnival in the works
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Kia is apparently planning a battery-electric EV7 and a hydrogen-powered van from the Carnival series, which is available in certain markets. This is according to a Korean portal citing an internal company document that lists production plans for the coming years.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz starts assembling electric GLC in India
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Mercedes-Benz has begun assembling the electric GLC from imported knocked-down kits at its plant in Chakan, near Pune in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Chakan is the second site for assembling the new EV from kits, after Thailand's Thonburi Automotive Assembly Plant (TAAP), and overall its fourth production site worldwide.

item.title: Ireland unveils new charging infrastructure strategy for 2028
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Ireland aims to further expand its charging infrastructure by the end of 2028. A new national strategy includes additional fast-charging parks along major traffic routes and more charging options in residential areas.

item.title: LG Energy Solution launches battery research competition
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: LG Energy Solution launches the Battery Innovation Contest 2026. Universities and research institutions worldwide can submit proposals for new battery technologies until December 6. The focus includes battery materials, battery management, and AI.

item.title: PPC Blue to install fast chargers on Romanian motorway
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Greek charging provider PPC Blue continues to expand in Romania, and is now installing and operating 30 fast-charging points along Romanian highway A7 in cooperation with Romanian oil company Oscar Downstream. Nearly half of the charging points will be suitable for electric trucks and buses.

item.title: Fraunhofer develops tool for battery recycling
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Fraunhofer FFB and RWTH Aachen University have developed an evaluation model for the recycling of lithium-ion batteries. It allows different processes to be compared in terms of their costs and CO₂ emissions.

item.title: Tesla opens new engineering centre in Berlin-Köpenick
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Tesla has opened its new development center in Berlin-Köpenick. Engineers and technicians will work there on new vehicles, engines, and materials, as well as research and testing. The location will bring together 250 employees who previously worked at various sites.

item.title: Switzerland to align CO2 targets for vans and trucks with EU standards
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The Swiss Federal Council wants to align the CO2 requirements for newly registered trucks and vans with the EU targets. While this would relax the CO2 limits for light commercial vehicles starting in 2030, the regulations for trucks are to be tightened.

item.title: Are Europe’s truck manufacturers losing their home market?
item.dc:creator: Peter Schwierz
item.description: European commercial vehicle manufacturers now offer a wide range of electric trucks. However, new competitors from China and other regions are increasingly pressuring the established industry - not necessarily with better technology, but with lower prices. In a video interview with electrive, Johanna Braun from Transport & Environment (T&E) explains why she considers the demand for relaxing European CO₂ fleet limits to be the wrong strategy.

media:content.media:title: Are Europe’s truck manufacturers losing their home market? - electrive.com
media:content.media:description: Auf YouTube findest du die angesagtesten Videos und Tracks. Außerdem kannst du eigene Inhalte hochladen und mit Freunden oder gleich der ganzen Welt teilen.

item.title: EU Parliament: Environment Committee votes to relax CO2 rules
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Following the Industry and Transport Committee, the Environment Committee has now also voted in favour of relaxing the combustion engine phase-out. The European Parliament as a whole is expected to decide in December. The previous votes are considered an important indicator.

item.title: Factory logistics with 25-metre trucks: Fendt opts for longer electric HGVs
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Agricultural machinery manufacturer Fendt recently adopted a unique approach to electrifying its in-house logistics for tractor production. Alongside its partner Ansorge, the Bavarian company is using eight electric long-haul trucks to transport tractor cabs. Other companies, such as Elflein, are now also using these 25.25-meter-long e-trucks.

item.title: Charging hub opened at Melbourne Airport
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: BP Pulse has opened what it says is Australia’s largest EV charging hub at Melbourne Airport. The charging hub has 24 charging bays with both 150kW and 300kW chargers, including charging bays for trucks.

item.title: Clean Trucks Program launched in Illinois
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: In the USA, the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA) has launched its Clean Trucks Program with two major initiatives. The funding is meant to enable fleet operators in the state to replace older diesel trucks with electric alternatives.

item.title: Jungheinrich reveals electric forklifts made for the Asia Pacific region
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: German manufacturer Jungheinrich has announced the Asia-Pacific launch of its next generation of EFG MB and EFG MC electric counterbalance forklifts. The three-wheel EFG MB covers load capacities from 1.6 to 2.0 tonnes and is designed for manoeuvrability in confined spaces. The four-wheel EFG MC covers load capacities from 2.0 to 3.0 tonnes.

item.title: Struggling electric bus manufacturer Ebusco secures €12 million
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Dutch electric bus manufacturer Ebusco is receiving a capital injection of a total of twelve million euros from five existing investors. The sum is intended to finance operations until the second quarter of 2027. Shortly before, Ebusco had to postpone the payment of October salaries due to its strained liquidity situation.

item.title: ABB and Oreve expand truck charging network in France
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: ABB E-mobility and Oreve are expanding their collaboration in building public truck charging infrastructure in France. By the end of 2028, twelve new locations are being established with around 100 charging points and a total of 18 MW of charging power. The first MCS-capable facility is planned for 2027.

item.title: Waymo robotaxis occupy public charging stations in US cities in droves
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Electric car drivers in some major US cities report that Waymo's robotaxis are regularly occupying public charging stations. "They come in droves," a resident told the Los Angeles Times. Cases have been reported in San Diego, Nashville, and St. Louis, among others.

item.title: Cabify fleet grows to 320 all-electric Škoda Elroq models
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: In the Spanish cities of Barcelona and Seville, mobility company Cabify is deploying 200 new Skoda Elroq vehicles. 120 of these models have already been in operation in Madrid since 2025. As part of the 2030 decarbonization plan, all of Cabify's vehicles are set to be emission-free.

item.title: Honda announces Alpha EV in India, effectively scrapping 0 Series
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Honda has announced Alpha as the final name of its first electric car for India. Evolving from the '0 α (alpha)', a near-production prototype unveiled at the 2025 Japan Mobility Show, the new EV will compete with the Hyundai Creta Electric, Mahindra BE 6, Tata Sierra.ev, Maruti Suzuki e Vitara, and Toyota Urban Cruiser Ebella in India.

item.title: 12-metre autonomous electric bus running tests with passengers in Munich
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The MINGA project —short for "Munich's automated public transport with ridepooling, solo buses, and bus platoons"— is about to reach a decisive milestone: Starting November 17, test users will be able to ride in an autonomous electric MAN bus. Over 2,000 people have made pre-registrations for a test ride so far.

item.title: Mercedes Power Converter decouples high-voltage supply from battery state
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Mercedes is developing new technology to constantly provide a voltage of 800 volts in electric vehicles. With current technology, the system voltage is directly dependent on the state of the battery cells. In the future, Mercedes wants to use a so-called Power Converter that bypasses this dependency through individual micro-converters per cell unit.

item.title: BYD and Iberdrola launch joint charging offer in Spain
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: BYD, in partnership with energy provider Iberdrola, is offering a comprehensive electric mobility package for the Spanish market. When purchasing an electric vehicle or plug-in hybrid from the brand, customers now receive an incentive package including a wallbox, a special electricity tariff, and discounts for home and public charging.

item.title: BMW Brilliance workforce reports 1,800 layoffs in China
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: According to reports from Chinese media, the BMW Brilliance joint venture began layoffs in China on 2 November, 2026. Employees are said to have discussed a scope of around 1,800 redundancies, which corresponds to approximately 9.5 per cent of the BMW Brilliance workforce. The German carmaker has not yet made a public statement on the matter.

item.title: How rare earth elements can be upcycled from magnets
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Technology that enables the recovery of rare earth elements such as neodymium from magnets is being developed in the NEO-CYCLE project in Germany with researchers from the Fraunhofer IKTS and TU Bergakademie Freiberg. Such magnets are used, among other things, in electric vehicles and wind turbines, and through these new technologies, can be upcycled in Europe for other industries, including pharmaceuticals and the hydrogen economy.

item.title: Turkish electric carmaker Togg plans third model for June 2027
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Togg plans to expand its lineup in June 2027 with a more affordable model. The company plans to offer the T6X at a significantly lower price than the existing T10X and T10F models.
